## Natural history notes

A small crambid moth characterized by pale tan to yellowish wings marked with translucent patches, dark lines, and warm brown shading that can give the wings a stained-glass appearance. In Florida, it is found in wetlands, marsh edges, ponds, canals, ditches, gardens, and other humid open habitats where aquatic or moisture-loving vegetation is present. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on wetland plants, often living among leaves or tied plant material and helping connect marsh vegetation with the broader insect food web.
